archetype.name: Dual-Threat (pocket-leaning)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose legs have long ranked among the league's best at the position and still pay off on scrambles, but whose 2026 value came mostly from intermediate and deep throws rather than designed runs.

report.headline: Good downfield, broken underneath, and now on IR behind a struggling offense
report.take:
Hurts has spent his career as a top-tier rushing quarterback with an efficient, careful arm. His rush yards ranked between 1st and 9th in every season, and he posted a CPOE of 7.5 in 2024, first in the league. The 2026 version is harder to read. Through five games of logged stats (six starts) he sits at -0.025 EPA per dropback, essentially league average, on a 2-3 record. He is now on injured reserve and listed as QB4, and Tanner McKee and Joe Milton III have started since.

The season splits in two. On throws of 10+ air yards he was excellent: 0.739 EPA per attempt, a CPOE of 8.7 and six of his eight touchdowns. Under 10 air yards he was one of the worst passers around: -0.273 EPA per attempt and a -7.1 CPOE. Screens and throws behind the line returned -0.693 EPA with a 9.1% success rate. That is not how Hurts has played before. His bad-throw rate jumped to 21.4% (43rd of 45) from 14.3% last year, and his completion rate fell seven points. An offense ranked dead last in success rate gave him little, but his own short-area accuracy was the bigger problem.

The averages also hide the schedule. He opened against Washington and Tennessee, defenses that now rank 20th and 30th, and was fine. Then he faced Chicago, the Rams and Jacksonville (7th, 4th and 2nd today) and lost all three. Over that stretch he managed -0.148 EPA per dropback and a -9.9 CPOE. Some of the slide is opponent quality, but the accuracy drop is too steep to blame on schedule alone.

On the positive side, he held up well under pressure by his own standards. His pressure-to-sack rate of 27.1% is better than in most of his seasons, and his 12 scrambles were worth 0.307 EPA apiece. The designed-run game was the opposite: 1.11 yards a carry and stuffed more than half the time. Whether he returns depends on a timeline the dossier doesn't give, and the top receiver from his starts, Dontayvion Wicks, is also on IR now.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep accuracy held
strengths.body: Beyond 10 air yards he completed throws well above expectation and produced most of his touchdowns. The 10-19 yard band alone added 23.5 EPA. This fits his career: he has consistently been an efficient play-action and intermediate passer. The 46-attempt sample is small, but it matches who he has been.

strengths.title: Scrambles still create value
strengths.body: When plays broke down he got out and gained yards. His scrambles averaged 0.307 EPA and moved the chains five times. That legs-as-outlet trait has followed him his whole career and is the most durable part of his game.

strengths.title: Fewer sacks off pressure than usual
strengths.body: His 27.1% pressure-to-sack rate is mid-pack and clearly better than his 2024 and 2022 marks. That came despite a time to throw over three seconds, so he extended plays without paying for it in sacks the way he sometimes has.

concerns.title: Short-area accuracy fell apart
concerns.body: Throws under 10 air yards were a net drain, and a 21.4% bad-throw rate sits near the bottom of the league. That rate was 7.1 points worse than last year. Hurts has posted a positive CPOE every year since 2021, so this is either something physical (he is now on IR) or a genuine slump. Either way it is the main thing that has to change if he returns.

concerns.title: Collapse against good defenses
concerns.body: His last three logged games came against top-seven defenses. He went 0-3 with a -9.9 CPOE and -0.148 EPA per dropback. Part of that is schedule, but the Rams game (12 of 27, 36% bad throws) was poor by any standard.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate and fumble luck
concerns.body: He scored five touchdowns on 14 red-zone attempts, and his 5.2% TD rate is above the league norm while his yards per attempt is not. That will likely cool. He also had three turnover-worthy fumbles and lost none, a bounce that won't keep going his way.

trend.note: He was solid against weak defenses in Weeks 1-2. He then slid through three straight losses to top-seven units, with completion rate, CPOE and EPA all sinking, before landing on injured reserve.

nextGame.headline: On IR: a soft Dallas defense he won't get to face
nextGame.body:
On paper this is exactly the defense his profile wants. Dallas ranks last in defensive EPA and 30th against the pass, and it is 28th on short throws, the area where Hurts struggled most. It also lets opposing WR1s beat their averages more than any other team. Offenses run against Dallas more than usual, and its run defense ranks last, which would suit his scrambles and the Eagles' backs. The Book still has Philadelphia as an 8.5-point road underdog on a four-day turnaround, which reflects the Eagles' current quarterback situation more than the matchup.

The problem is availability. Hurts is on injured reserve and sits fourth on the depth chart, so he isn't expected to play. On his side, McKee is questionable with a rib injury, Wicks is on IR, and Goedert and Barkley are both limited. On the Dallas side, starting corner DaRon Bland is on IR and both safeties are out, which thins a secondary that was already allowing big passing games. Whoever starts at quarterback for Philadelphia gets the benefit, not Hurts.

keyMatchups.title: Dallas can't defend the short game
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows 0.185 EPA on short passes, 28th in the league. Hurts lost value exactly there this year. If he were active, this would be the best spot of his season to get the underneath game working again.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Dallas secondary
keyMatchups.body: Bland is on IR, and safeties Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke are out. Combined with a defense ranked 32nd overall, the Philadelphia passing game should find openings regardless of who is under center.

keyMatchups.title: Eagles quarterback availability
keyMatchups.body: McKee is questionable with sore ribs, and Milton started the last two games. Hurts' status matters only if he returns from IR, which is not expected this week.

nextGame.watch: Any word on Hurts' activation from IR. Until he returns, the quarterback depth chart belongs to McKee and Milton.

restOfSeason.body:
The dossier gives no return date, so any outlook depends on whether he gets back on the field. If he does, expect roughly his early-season form rather than the late slide. His intermediate and deep game and his scrambling are long-standing traits. His sub-60% completion rate and huge bad-throw rate are far outside his career norms and should move back toward them, especially against weaker defenses than Chicago, the Rams and Jacksonville. His red-zone touchdown efficiency is the part most likely to regress.

The environment limits the upside. The offense is bottom-five in EPA and last in success rate, it passes less than expected, and its most productive target, Wicks, is on IR until mid-December. Over a full healthy stretch, a reasonable expectation is something like 170-215 passing yards and 15-28 rushing yards a game, with touchdowns closer to one a game than the pace from his first two weeks.
swingFactors: Timing and health of his return from IR
Whether short-area accuracy returns to career norms

confidence.note: On IR with no return date, QB4 on the depth chart, and a five-game sample split between weak and elite defenses.
